summary: Drawer inbox. New ui/SwitcherDrawer.kt: SwitcherInbox groups the host's sessions (one per project) into Needs you (pending approvals) / Running (accepted or running prompt, running worker task, or live desktop stream) / Idle, in that order with host order kept inside a group and empty groups omitted; pendingApprovals() sums approvals across projects. SwitcherDrawer renders the grouped inbox (one 48dp row per session: title, session name, approval badge, single spoken summary, selected state) followed by the project and worktree management that used to sit on the main screen: project tabs, Open/Close workspace, worktree/directory tabs with add/remove/rename/move and concurrency, all moved unchanged (same testTags, content descriptions and enable fences). AppShell hosts it in a ModalNavigationDrawer opened from a top-bar menu button badged with the pending-approval count; choosing an inbox row switches project and closes the drawer. The main screen keeps only the session toolbar (WorkspaceTabs.kt renamed SessionToolbar.kt). Goldens: drawer_<cell>.png for the 8 portrait cells; main_<cell>.png re-recorded (tabs left the main screen, menu badge added).

(2) To keep the instrumentation suites unchanged (all use the PairingScreen lambda adapter and click project/worktree controls directly; WorkspaceModelTest, SessionScopeScreenTest and WorkerScreenTest do too), the PairingScreen adapter passes AppShell(inlineSwitcher = true), which renders the same SwitcherDrawer content inline above the workspace instead of in the modal drawer; production (MainActivity -> AppShell) uses the modal drawer, which the Robolectric drawer test exercises. Inbox rows use clearAndSetSemantics with a summary description and testTag inbox-<id> so they never collide with the tabs' text/tag selectors. (3) Group labels are English (Needs you / Running / Idle) to match the rest of the app's English UI. The project tab row remains in the drawer as the management view next to the inbox.
